title: ZTF spot rotation, calibrated with seven open clusters, shows no excess of active stars among 91 dust dimmers; the few rotating extreme-dust dwarfs are young association members
abstract: Question: are main-sequence dust dimmers and extreme-dust field dwarfs young or magnetically active? Prior campaign ages came from kinematics only, and UV and X-ray tests had little power at 1-2 kpc. Approach: one ZTF DR24 rotation search (high-pass filter, dip clipping, Lomb-Scargle, g/r or half-split consistency, alias and same-quadrant vetoes) for 91 dimmers (81 TZ25 dippers, 10 campaign dimmers), 331 dwarfs with a confirmed extreme 12 um excess, 3,491 matched controls on the same ZTF CCD quadrants, and 1,576 members of seven open clusters (125 Myr to 4 Gyr) as age calibrators. Injections measured sensitivity. Results: the detected fraction falls from 0.40 (Pleiades) and 0.20 (M34) to 0.005 (M67); field controls give 0.0095. Dimmers: 3 of 91 rotate, 1.2 expected (p = 0.11). Fewer than 10.5 percent of TZ25 dippers have a 0.5-10 d spot signal of 2 percent or more (95 percent). The fraction younger than about 250 Myr is below 0.62, a weak limit because young F/G stars seldom show ZTF spots. Gaia20cdd and G2870 have no spot signal of 1 percent or more; six deep dimmers cannot be tested because of dips. TESS shows no stable period in G2874 or G4466. Extreme-dust dwarfs: unblended 4 of 114 rotate (4.8 expected), blends 0 of 196 (2.4). The six dusty rotators are kinematically young (mean p_young 0.41 against 0.07; colour-stratified p = 0.037) and four lie in the Orion complex; a post hoc box holds 15 of 213 unblended and 0 of 738 blended stars (p = 1e-10). Other young ones lie towards Taurus, Sco-Cen and the TW Hya association. Conclusion: spot rotation gives no sign that dimmers are young or active, in agreement with their field kinematics. The kinematically young part of the extreme-dust sample is mainly pre-main-sequence association stars with primordial discs, so genuine extreme dust around mature dwarfs is rarer than the unblended count. Limitations: ZTF needs 1-2 percent spots; the cluster calibration uses other fields and approximate reddening; the Orion box is post hoc.
